articles.title: Pulse Market Insight #310
articles.summary: Dry conditions and slow planting in India are weighing on the outlook for its gram and yellow pea crops, which could boost import demand for Canadian yellow peas, especially in the second half of 2026/27. Lentil planting in India is running ahead of last year and average, but a record Australian red lentil crop poses a risk to Canadian red lentil sales. Yellow pea prices are strengthening on Indian and Chinese buying, while green lentil prices have recovered from harvest lows and show more strength than red lentils.

articles.title: Pulse Market Insight #309
articles.summary: Pea exports are running strongly, with the 2026/27 program now looking achievable and pea bids firming, especially for yellows. Lentil exports are slightly lower, lentil deliveries from farmers are lagging, and lentil rallies have paused, with red lentils showing little price response. The article advises sellers to be patient with yellow peas, expects modest gains for green lentils, and expects only modest prospects for red lentils.

articles.title: Pulse Market Insight #308
articles.summary: India's pulse demand is pushing prices higher for Canadian peas and lentils. A weak southwest monsoon is damaging the tur (pigeon pea) crop, so Indian buyers are importing more green lentils as a substitute, and tur, green lentil, and yellow pea prices have all risen. Imports of lentils and peas are running well above last year, and the bigger demand for red lentils and yellow peas may come later with the winter rabi crop and possible tariff cuts, while record Australian red lentil supplies and large Canadian green lentil stocks limit how far prices can rise.

articles.title: Pulse Market Insight #307
articles.summary: Canadian pulse supplies for 2026/27 look comfortable, so demand is the bigger factor, and early signals are strong. China and India are both buying Canadian peas, China's imports are at record levels, and India's pea and lentil imports are running well ahead of last year. Rising Indian prices and a possible monsoon-driven shortfall could push prices higher, though a record Australian red lentil crop is a limiting factor.

articles.title: Pulse Market Insight #306
articles.summary: Canadian pulse crops are expected to be smaller in 2026 due to lower acreage and yields, which should support prices in 2026/27 alongside strong export demand for peas, lentils, and chickpeas. The main offset is record-large carryover stocks from 2025/26, which keep total supplies close to last year's levels for peas and lentils and could erase the impact of the smaller chickpea crop. Dry bean supplies are also down, and prices are already rallying.

articles.title: Pulse Market Insight #305 – September 4, 2026
articles.summary: Black Sea shipping disruptions are limiting exports from Russia and another major exporter just as importers buy new-crop supplies, pushing demand toward Canada. Pea supplies were already tightening, with the largest production declines in Canada and Russia, and yellow pea prices in Mumbai jumped more than US$50 per tonne in late August. The article expects supportive prices for growers this fall, especially for yellow peas, though it cautions that shipping barriers could ease quickly and that green peas and green lentils will face carryover limits on rallies.

articles.title: Pulse Market Insight #304 – August 21, 2026
articles.summary: The article says the 2026 pulse harvest in western Canada is running slow, and the market is split: yellow peas and red lentils face tighter supplies and strong export prospects, while green peas and green lentils are weighed down by large carryover stocks. Indian monsoon rainfall, which is currently below average, is a key factor for demand, and prices are expected to recover from harvest lows, though green pulse rallies may be good times to sell.

articles.title: Pulse Market Insight #303 – July 24, 2026
articles.summary: Indian monsoon rains have been erratic and are still 16% below average, slowing tur planting and threatening both kharif and rabi pulse crops. Desi chickpea prices have risen to their highest since early 2025, while tur, yellow pea, and red lentil prices have not yet responded much, likely because India has comfortable supplies. If the rains stay weak, supply shortfalls could lift prices and raise demand for Canadian pulses, though analysts advise patience for now.

articles.title: Pulse Market Insight #302 – July 14, 2026
articles.summary: The article reports that pulse acreage fell this year, with yellow peas down 16% and total lentils down 11%, and that wet soil raises yield risk. These supply cuts, along with strong expected demand from China and India and a small U.S. dry bean crop, point toward firmer prices later, especially for yellow peas and red lentils. Current western Canadian bids are still drifting sideways to lower, so the author suggests growers be patient with new-crop sales.

articles.title: Pulse Market Insight #301 – June 26, 2026
articles.summary: Western Canada's weather has swung from drought worries to excess moisture, which threatens pulse crops like peas, lentils and chickpeas through disease and lower yields. Because yield and acreage are uncertain, the author suggests farmers hold off on new sales, since pulse bids historically fall in early summer and tend to recover after harvest. Demand factors, especially India's uncertain pulse production, could also make waiting a wise choice.
